title: LongStream attention stitching and tenant-aware eviction playbook for mixed v2/v3 workloads
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem statement: Long-context streaming workloads cause repeated kernel switches between FlashAttention v2 and v3 in the serving runtime. For mixed-precision models and multi-tenant racks this produces excessive ephemeral workspace allocations, KV cache churn, and increased tail latency during prefill->decode transitions. We observed cases where per-request latency spiked 25-40% and OOM or eviction activity increased under bursty traffic patterns.

Goal: Reduce memory churn and tail latency for long-context streaming by: 1) introducing an attention stitcher that preserves intermediate tile layouts across kernel boundaries; 2) implementing a tenant-aware eviction policy that prefers reclaiming ephemeral workspace versus KV cache when doing short-term capacity compaction; and 3) adding targeted telemetry and microbenchmarks to detect regressions early.

Proposed approach:
- Attention stitching layer: a lightweight translator that runs during prefill end / decode start to reconcile v2 layout -> v3 layout (and reverse) without reserializing whole KV blobs. The stitcher will: 1) surface a minimal per-layer diff plan (tile reordering + padding adjustments), 2) opportunistically use inplace rearrange kernels when memory permits, otherwise schedule incremental compaction passes. This reduces full-copy fallback.
- Workspace pooling + eviction hierarchy: implement a tiered reclaim strategy in runtime allocator: Tier A (ephemeral workspaces tied to kernel op, reclaimable), Tier B (short-lived decode buffers), Tier C (KV cache pinned by tenant SLA). The eviction controller will consider tenant priority, recent access heat, and an estimated cost of reconstructing a shard. For low-priority tenants we will prefer reclaiming Tier A/B to avoid degrading higher-priority KV caches.
- Warmup continuity: add a fast prober that keeps a tiny set of warmed kernels (v2/v3) for expected long-stream sessions to avoid expensive kernel reloading on first decode chunk. Prober decisions will be guided by recent-start histograms and per-tenant median sequence lengths.
- Telemetry: add instrumentation (metrics and spans) for (a) stitch time per layer, (b) workspace reclaim events by tier, (c) percent of stitch-inplace vs copy fallback, (d) end-to-end prefill->decode latency delta, and (e) eviction-induced error rates. Surface these in a new dashboard and SLO guard.

Experimental plan:
- Unit microbench harnesses for synthetic long sequences across shapes (1024, 4096, 16384) and batch mixes. Measure memory allocations, copies, and latency percentiles.
- Canary rollout: staged rollout with config flag `attn_stitcher=v1` behind runtime feature flag. Start on a single low-risk rack with mixed tenants; run for 48 hours and compare baseline histograms.
- Regression tests: add fuzzed tiling cases where v2 -> v3 stride/pad mismatches historically triggered copy fallback. Gate merges with an automated replay test that runs production-like traces in CI.

Acceptance criteria:
- 90th percentile prefill->decode latency reduced by >= 15% for long-context sessions (>= 4k tokens) on canary racks.
- Global ephemeral workspace allocations down by >= 20% under synthetic multi-tenant bursts.
- No increase in customer-facing error rate (>=99.95% success) for canary tenants.

Rollout and rollback:
- Rollout stages: feature flag on -> canary rack 1 -> canary rack 3 -> 25% traffic -> 100% traffic. Each stage requires 24-48h observation window.
- Rapid rollback path: config toggle to disable stitcher and trigger a controlled KV cache warm-rebuild; keep previous kernel warmset preserved for 5 minutes to reduce cold latency.

Open implementation tasks: list of concrete subtasks.
- Implement layout-diff generator and small inplace rearrange kernels (ENG-807778).
- Extend allocator to support tier labels and reclamation hooks (ENG-807779).
- Instrument metrics and dashboard (ENG-807780).
- Add CI replay fuzz tests and microbench suite (ENG-807781).

Notes on trade-offs: Stitching avoids copying but adds CPU work; we must ensure stitch CPU cost doesn't regress under tiny-batch latencysensitive workloads. The tenancy-aware eviction improves multitenant fairness but requires careful tuning for SLA-bound customers.

Security & compliance: No new customer data export. Stitcher operates on in-memory key-values and must maintain existing encryption-at-rest / KMS bindings.

Related docs and references: internal perf notes, flashattn upstream issues, prior regression tickets (see dependencies).
